title: Split the Array to Make Coprime Products
summary: Given an integer array nums, determine the smallest index i where the product of the first i+1 elements and the product of the remaining elements are coprime.
statement: Given an integer array nums, determine the smallest index i where the product of the first i+1 elements and the product of the remaining elements are coprime. If no valid split exists, return -1. Two numbers are considered coprime if their greatest common divisor is 1.
constraints: Split after index i with both sides nonempty.
The products of the two sides must have greatest common divisor one.
Return the smallest valid i, or -1.
hints: A split is valid exactly when no prime factor appears on both sides.
Record the last index containing each prime factor.
Scan left to right while extending the farthest required endpoint for factors seen so far.
The first index equal to that farthest endpoint closes every active prime interval, and therefore is the earliest coprime split.
editorial: The first index equal to that farthest endpoint closes every active prime interval, and therefore is the earliest coprime split.

tests.explanation: After index two, left primes are two and seven while right primes are three and five, so the products are coprime.
Every split shares at least one prime across the boundary.
